newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's TV Azteca seeks 35 pct of TV ad market.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's TV Azteca seeks 35 pct of TV ad market.

text.p: Mexico's second-biggest private television network Television Azteca has grabbed 20 percent of the country's lucrative TV advertising market and is aiming for 35 percent, a company official said on Wednesday.
"In 1996 we will end the year with 20 percent market share," Gustavo Guzman, Azteca's vice president of sales, told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Azteca was privatised barely two years ago and is now run by Ricardo Salinas Pliego, who also owns consumer electronics company Grupo Elektra.

Azteca has signed up 50 of the 400 biggest spenders on television advertising for next year, Guzman said. The Mexican market is worth more than $5 billion a year, most of it going to media giant Grupo Televisa.
"Of the 400 advertisers you can get in Mexico for television, we have reached agreements for 1997 in 50 cases," Guzman said.
"The thing is to get 35 percent of the market, because there is enough for everyone," he said.
